labels.notes: The label is unmarked and the row is partial, which is correct. The module docstring writes `cor:yamabe` — `perforated.tex:929`, the \begin{corollary} line, within the first 4000 characters and without the ``**`label`**`` mark. No bold string in the file matches tools/ledger.py's mark regex: the bold SCOPE headings at l.80–106 contain no `prefix:` label. I read the six anchors against perforated l.913–939, hypothesis by hypothesis. (1) « closed N-manifold, complement of n balls »: hN, finite vol and bvol, vol ≠ 0, ∃ j, bvol j ≠ 0 (DEC-186). On a manifold reading: CompactSpace, ConnectedSpace, μ ≠ 0, ∃ j, σ j ≠ 0. (2) « σ(Σ̄) ≤ 0, constant scalar curvature, minimal boundary, B_j conformally round »: hRc (R_g x = c for all x), MinimalBoundary, and the lem:gluing family with a GluingInput per τ (y_nonpos is σ(Σ̄) ≤ 0). These are exactly the hypotheses of the strict upper_bound_of_gluings_of_pos and thm_lower_bound*. Nothing restricts Σ̄ to a torus, so on topology the anchors are broader than « on a punctured torus ». (3) eq:yamabe-upper (« a gluing estimate gives ») is a conclusion. Its λ_∂ > 0 is derived from eq:main through Fq_one_pos and Λ_max ≥ 1, and is not carried. (4) « Theorem thm:main converts »: thm:main's hypotheses are carried on the model and disclosed (MeanPoincare, TraceBound, InteriorBump, StarIneq/StarIneqSigned with any real Ã, AbsLatticeApprox in cor_yamabe only). The _three and _starN forms discharge eq:star from valid λ, C. The Mfd.Reads forms discharge MeanPoincare, the trace bound and eq:star at λ₁, C_SP, and carry NonConst and InteriorBump. Each anchor's hypothesis list matches its strict thm_lower_bound* counterpart one to one: I compared all six, including the `let A` of the _three and _starN forms. The one exception is that hσb : 0 ≤ σb becomes hYb : σb = 0. (5) δ := Yb(Σ) − Y_[g](Σ) is gapYb σb g = σb − M.Y g, proved equal to the strict gapBdry through the strict EH = Y. Yb(Σ) is not definable on the model (kb 0083), so it is a real parameter. « For a punctured flat torus Yb(Σ) = 0 » is carried as hYb : σb = 0. That hypothesis is satisfiable, and it is disclosed as a reading of an unproved assertion (finding 1, OQ-121 (a)/(c)). Every other conjunct is stated for every value s of Yb. (6) Conclusions. « |R_g| Vol^{2/N} = δ » is |c|·V^{2/N} = gapYb σb g, with c < 0 derived. The F form θ/(1+θ)·F_g(1)·(1 + corRem) ≤ gapYb σb g is unconditional, and it is also ≤ λ_∂ and > 0. The printed M form, θ/(1+θ)·2(N−1)M/V^{(N−2)/N}·(1 + corRem) ≤ δ, is a conjunct conditional on round areas with M = roundMass N r (OQ-44 as ruled by DEC-186: disclosed, finding 2). « 1 + O(F_g(1)) » is the explicit 1 + corRem. I checked that 1 + corRem = ((1+θ)/θ)/Λ_max(1/θ, 1, ÃF/a_N) by unfolding mainRem (Main.lean:238), so the factor is exactly eq:main's θ/(1+θ)·(1+corRem) = 1/Λ_max and nothing is lost. The O(F) is stated as IsBigO at fixed θ, Ã, with the uniform 3/7 bound (OQ-111 (b)). The reading is named, and an existential O(·) would be vacuous for one (Σ, g). « θ → 1 for Schwarzschild collars » is not formalized and is disclosed (T-perf-dilute-limit). (7) corConst_tendsto_half: along any filter, θ → 1 and Ã·F → 0 give θ/(1+θ)(1 + corRem) → 1/2. This is the implication « so the constant is 1/2 » needs, and it is neither vacuous nor trivially true. The hypotheses are satisfiable (θ ≡ 1, A ≡ 0, any filter), and the proof needs the uniform remainder bound. At A ≡ 0, corRem ≡ 0 (Λ_max(1/θ,1,0) = 1 + 1/θ), so it contains the bare-coefficient reading θ/(1+θ) → 1/2 as a special case. Its premise θ → 1 is not proved, and the REPORT says so. Reuse (CAMPAIGN): cor_yamabe_of_eq_main calls the strict upper_bound_of_gluings_of_pos and lower_bound_of_eq_main (it reads c < 0, EH = Y, κF > 0 and the round-area identity from the latter). eq_main_cor_identity rewrites the strict eq_main_asymp_identity, and corRem_le_uniform builds on the strict mainRem_le_uniform. The anchors obtain eq:main from the strict eq_main_lattice, eq_main_signed, star3_of_consts, starN_signed_of_consts and the Reads lemmas. No strict statement is re-proved; the new arithmetic (s + λ_∂ ≤ gapYb s g, |c|V^{2/N} = −Y) is linarith from strict conclusions. Non-vacuity: toy_cor_yamabe applies the principal anchor cor_yamabe itself, not the _signed form. Its inputs are the strict toy data (toyConst (−8), constant gluing family, toyNegInput, AbsLattice.approx of toy_absLattice, star3AtilCorr at λ = 4, C = 1, σb = 0), and the kernel accepts it, so the principal anchor's hypotheses are jointly satisfiable and the bound is strictly positive. The Mfd.Reads forms are not witnessed with a gluing family, as in the strict file; the REPORT claims no such witness. Bookkeeping: the label's decls list (15) includes helpers and the toy witness. REPORT.notes names the six anchors plus corConst_tendsto_half as ledger decls; curate those.

findings_check: Finding 1 (Yb(Σ) = 0 asserted, proved nowhere) is true. In the companion, Yb occurs only at l.915, l.924–926 and the macro definition. « For a punctured flat torus Yb(Σ)=0 » (l.925–926) has no proof or citation; the AB citation at l.916 is for the definition. The section is for a closed N-manifold, N general. The only counterpart, yamabe's eq:sigma-torus (Yamabegap l.365–369), is for Σ̄ = T³ only and is a one-sentence argument. Its lower half exhibits metrics of energy tending to zero. That bounds Y_[g] of their classes from above, while σ^∂ ≥ 0 needs a class whose infimum is ≥ −ε; T-yamabe-thm-lower-bound's AUDIT-1 records the same observation. The finding claims no counterexample and does not overreach.

Finding 2 (M undefined in the companion; the M form unproved for non-round B_j) is true. The companion's only M's are the manifold at l.287–288 and the 2×2 matrix at l.529–543. With yamabe's eq:mass-def and H_g = 0, M_j = −∫ H_ref = ∫ H_mean(∂C_j), since H_ref = −1/r_j is the mean, not the sum, of the principal curvatures. Minkowski's inequality ∫H_mean dA ≥ √(4πA) for convex C_j, with equality only for round spheres, together with c_3 = 4√(4π) (Yamabegap l.338), gives c_3|B_j|^{1/2} = 4√(4π|B_j|) ≤ 4M_j. Hence F_g(1) = c_3Σ|B_j|^{1/2}/Vol^{1/3} ≤ 4M/Vol^{1/3}, strictly if some B_j is not round. A shape-dependent ratio below 1 is not absorbed by 1 + O(F_g(1)) as the holes shrink at fixed shape. So the printed M bound does not follow from the argument. The REPORT states this as argued, not formalized, and calls the M form « unproved », not false.

Finding 3 (minor, the θ → 1 clause) is true as argued. prop:theta-examples (ii) is N = 3, the dilute limit, and the scalar-flat isotropic collar (1 + m/2s)⁴δ. The g of cor:yamabe has R_g ≡ c < 0, so it is not that metric. Under g' = u^{4/(N−2)}g, |∇v|²_{g'} dV_{g'} = u²|∇v|²_g dV_g, so θ is not conformally invariant. The REPORT labels this argued and routes it to T-perf-dilute-limit.

The two remarks are conjuncts of every anchor. One is the sign-free δ = Yb + |R_g|Vol^{2/N} ≥ Yb + λ_∂ ≥ Yb + θ/(1+θ)F(1+corRem). The other is corRem_le_uniform: |corRem| ≤ (3/7)|ÃF/a_N| for |ÃF/a_N| ≤ 1/4, for every θ > 0.

They are at least cor:yamabe in the named readings: Yb as a parameter σb with Yb = 0 carried (OQ-121), M = roundMass conditionally (OQ-44/DEC-186), O(F) = corRem (OQ-111 (b)), and thm:main's forms (OQ-109, OQ-118, OQ-93). Every reading is disclosed and the row is partial and unmarked. Nothing strict is re-proved. The toy witness instantiates the principal anchor. corConst_tendsto_half is a non-vacuous implication. The paper findings are true and are worded as argued where they are not formalized. Scope: only the dispatched file and the campaign directory.
